title: Daily Life - Going To The Bakery
audio: mp3/329. Daily Life - Going To The Bakery.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
My name is Marco.
My name is Catherine and today we're going to buy some food at a store for basically bread, right Marco?
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们要在商店买一些食物，基本上是面包，对吧，马可？

segments.en: That's right.
Today we're going to a bakery.
segments.zh: 今天我们要去一家面包店。

segments.en: So, this is basically a shop where they sell bread and different types of bread actually.
segments.zh: 所以，这基本上是一家商店，他们实际上出售面包和不同类型的面包。

segments.en: That's right.
So, we're going to learn all about these different kinds of bread.
segments.zh: 所以，我们将了解所有这些不同种类的面包。

segments.en: Let's take a listen to our dialogue.
Welcome to Al's Bakery.
What can I get you?
Hi, let me get a dozen croissants, four blueberry muffins and a loaf of sourdough bread.
segments.zh: 你好，我要一打牛角包、四个蓝莓玛芬和一条酸种面包。

segments.en: Sure.
Would you like to have the loaf sliced?
No, that's okay.
Do you have any whole wheat bread?
Oh, we're out at the moment.
May I suggest some rye bread?
Sure, that sounds good.
Do you have any cakes?
We have various birthday cakes and also some ice cream cakes.
segments.zh: 我们有各种生日蛋糕和一些冰淇淋蛋糕。

segments.en: I'll just take a cheesecake.
Will that be all?
Yes.
Your total is $43.20.
All right, we're back.
So, now let's take a look at some vocab on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以，现在让我们来看看一些关于语言要点的词汇。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
In Language Takeaway today we have many different kinds of bread.
segments.zh: 在今天的语言要点中，我们有许多不同种类的面包。

segments.en: The first kind actually comes to English from the French language.
segments.zh: 第一种实际上来自法语。

segments.en: We have croissants.
That's right, croissants.
Now, as you say, this is a type of bread that comes from France, I guess.
segments.zh: 现在，正如你所说，这是一种来自法国的面包，我猜。

segments.en: That's right.
It's really delicious.
It's buttery and flaky and it's in the shape of a crescent.
segments.zh: 它带着黄油香、口感酥松，呈新月形。

segments.en: So, it's like a curve, like a C. It kind of looks like also horns because it's got two little...
segments.zh: 所以，它就像一条曲线，像一个 C。它看起来也像角，因为它有两个小……

segments.en: It's got a horn on each side.
It does.
It does.
Many people like to eat this for breakfast in France, but you can find it everywhere in America at cafes and bakeries.
segments.zh: 许多人喜欢在法国吃这个当早餐，但你可以在美国的咖啡馆和面包店里到处都能找到它。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
So, those are croissants.
Now we're also buying blueberry muffins.
segments.zh: 现在我们也在购买蓝莓松饼。

segments.en: Okay, muffins are a delicious baked good.
segments.zh: 好吧，松饼是一种美味的烘焙食品。

segments.en: Blueberry muffins are the flavor, so we can also have strawberry or orange.
segments.zh: 蓝莓是口味，所以也可以是草莓味或橙子味。

segments.en: But in this case a muffin is kind of like a sweet baked good.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，松饼有点像甜烘焙食品。

segments.en: It's round.
So, it's kind of like a cake, like a little cake.
segments.zh: 所以，它有点像蛋糕，就像一个小蛋糕。

segments.en: It is like a little cake.
The top is bigger than the bottom.
So, the bottom you have some paper to hold on to and the top is round and maybe a little bit hard.
segments.zh: 所以，底部你有一些纸可以固定，顶部是圆形的，可能有点硬。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
So, those are muffins.
We'll post pictures of these on the site so you can see what they look like.
segments.zh: 我们将在网站上发布这些照片，以便您查看它们的外观。

segments.en: But moving on now, we have a type of bread.
segments.zh: 但现在继续，我们有一种面包。

segments.en: This is a sourdough bread.
All right.
So, there are many, many, many different kinds of breads, but sourdough is very unique because the flavor is a little bit sour.
segments.zh: 所以，有很多很多不同的面包，但酸面团很独特，因为味道有点酸。

segments.en: It's strong.
So, dough is the substance or what you use to make bread, right, or before bread is baked.
segments.zh: 所以，面团是你用来做面包的物质或东西，对，或者在烤面包之前。

segments.en: That's right.
So, before you make bread, it's kind of like a liquid.
segments.zh: 所以，在你做面包之前，它有点像液体。

segments.en: You have some milk or water that you mix with flour, so you have to hold it in a bowl or a cup.
segments.zh: 你有一些牛奶或水与面粉混合，所以你必须把它放在碗或杯子里。

segments.en: And after you bake it, it becomes hard.
So, dough is when it's soft and like a liquid.
segments.zh: 所以，面团是柔软的，像液体一样。

segments.en: Right.
You've seen it when they're making bread.
segments.zh: 当他们做面包的时候，你已经看到了。

segments.en: They have this, it looks like a paste sometimes and then it becomes hard or when they're making pizzas that's called dough.
segments.zh: 他们做的时候，有时看起来像糊状，然后变硬；他们做披萨时，那个也叫面团。

segments.en: And sour, obviously, because it has that flavor that you said, a very strong sour flavor.
segments.zh: 很酸，很明显，因为它有你说的那种味道，一种非常强烈的酸味。

segments.en: That's right.
And a different kind of bread that we might find is whole wheat bread.
segments.zh: 我们可能会发现另一种面包是全麦面包。

segments.en: Okay.
Now, this is like the healthy choice.
segments.zh: 现在，这就像健康的选择。

segments.en: Yes, it's normally the healthy choice.
segments.zh: 是的，这通常是健康的选择。

segments.en: That's because the flour that we put in the dough is whole wheat flour.
segments.zh: 那是因为我们放在面团里的面粉是全麦面粉。

segments.en: It's a little bit healthier.
It's actually a little bit darker than white flour, so it'll be brown.
segments.zh: 它其实比白面粉深一点，所以是棕色的。

segments.en: So, yeah, it's basically the brown bread.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，它基本上是黑面包。

segments.en: I think if you've noticed when you go to the store and you can get bread, you'll find one that looks white on the inside and this one actually looks brown on the inside.
segments.zh: 我想如果你注意到当你去商店时可以买到面包，你会发现里面的一种看起来是白色的，而这个实际上在里面看起来是棕色的。

segments.en: That's right.
And an even more brown colored bread, maybe even black, is rye bread.
segments.zh: 一个更棕色的面包，甚至可能是黑色的，是黑麦面包。

segments.en: So, what is rye?
Rye is another kind of grain and when you bake this rye bread, it has a very strong flavor and it's very, very dark, almost black.
segments.zh: 黑麦是另一种谷物，当你烘烤这种黑麦面包时，它的味道非常强烈，非常非常黑，几乎是黑色的。

segments.en: It's actually my favorite kind of bread.
segments.zh: 它实际上是我最喜欢的面包。

segments.en: So, what does it taste like or what's the difference between whole wheat bread and rye bread?
segments.zh: 那么，它的味道是什么，或者全麦面包和黑麦面包有什么区别？

segments.en: Rye bread is much heavier.
It has a stronger flavor.
Whole wheat bread is lighter.
Okay.
Very good.
So, obviously, it may be a little bit difficult to understand the differences between the breads, but we'll post pictures on the site so you can see them.
segments.zh: 所以，很明显，理解面包之间的差异可能有点困难，但我们会在网站上发布图片，以便您看到它们。

segments.en: And also, well, you have to go out to the bakery and try them so you can taste the difference.
segments.zh: 而且，好吧，你必须去面包店试一试，这样你才能品尝到不同的味道。

segments.en: That's right.
All right.
So, now let's move on to language takeaway part two and talk about a little bit more of the other vocab found in this lesson.
segments.zh: 所以，现在让我们继续讨论第二部分的语言要点，并谈谈本课中发现的更多其他词汇。

segments.en: Welcome to Al's Bakery.
What can I get you?
Hi.
Let me get a dozen croissants, four blueberry muffins, and a loaf of sourdough bread.
segments.zh: 让我买一打羊角面包、四个蓝莓松饼和一条酸面包。

segments.en: Sure.
Would you like to have the loaf sliced?
No, that's okay.
Do you have any whole wheat bread?
Oh, we're out at the moment.
May I suggest some rye bread?
Sure.
That sounds good.
Do you have any cakes?
We have various birthday cakes and also some ice cream cakes.
segments.zh: 我们有各种生日蛋糕和一些冰淇淋蛋糕。

segments.en: I'll just take a cheesecake.
Will that be all?
Yes.
Your total is $43.20.
So, when you want to go buy some bread or some baked goods, you have to know how to count those goods.
segments.zh: 所以，当你想去买一些面包或一些烘焙食品时，你必须知道如何计算这些商品。

segments.en: Okay, so today we have a couple of words to help you count bread.
segments.zh: 好的，所以今天我们有几句话可以帮助您数数面包。

segments.en: The first one we have is dozen.
segments.zh: 我们拥有的第一个词是 dozen（一打）。

segments.en: That's right.
So, for croissants, as you can see, it's a countable noun.
segments.zh: 所以，对于羊角面包来说，正如你所看到的，它是一个可数名词。

segments.en: And so, when you ask for a dozen croissants, you're asking for 12.
segments.zh: 所以，当你要十几个羊角面包时，你要的是 12 个羊角面包。

segments.en: That's right.
So, in English, the word dozen means 12.
segments.zh: 所以，在英语里，dozen 这个词的意思就是 12。

segments.en: You can buy a dozen eggs or in this case, a dozen blueberry muffins maybe.
segments.zh: 你可以买一打鸡蛋，或者在这种情况下，可能是一打蓝莓松饼。

segments.en: Okay.
So, it's a very popular term, a dozen or a half a dozen.
segments.zh: 所以，这是个很常用的说法，一打或半打。

segments.en: Sometimes people just buy six.
That's right.
So, half a dozen is six.
A whole dozen, just say dozen, is 12.
You can also have something special called a baker's dozen.
segments.zh: 还有一种特别的说法，叫做面包师的一打。

segments.en: Yes, I've heard about this.
What is a baker's dozen?
Well, a baker's dozen is basically a present the baker gives you.
segments.zh: 好吧，面包师的一打基本上是面包师白送你的一个。

segments.en: So, you buy 12, maybe 12 croissants and the baker gives you one more.
segments.zh: 所以，你买了 12 个，也许是 12 只羊角面包，面包师再给你一个。

segments.en: Wow, so you get 13.
Yes.
A baker's dozen is 13.
But do you ask for a baker's dozen or does the baker say, I'm going to give you the baker's dozen?
segments.zh: 但你是主动要面包师的一打，还是面包师说，我要多给你一个？

segments.en: I don't think I've ever asked for it.
segments.zh: 我想我从来没有要求过它。

segments.en: I think when I've bought bagels and I say I want a dozen bagels, they give me a baker's dozen.
segments.zh: 我想当我买百吉饼，说我要一打百吉饼时，他们会给我面包师的一打。

segments.en: They give me 13.
Okay.
So, when you're buying bread, now obviously you don't really buy a dozen sourdough breads.
segments.zh: 所以，当你买面包的时候，现在显然你并没有真正买到十几个酸面团面包。

segments.en: You buy a dozen loaves of sourdough bread.
segments.zh: 你买了十几个酸面团面包。

segments.en: So, the countable noun here is a loaf of bread.
segments.zh: 所以，这里的可数名词是一条面包。

segments.en: One loaf, two loaves.
Now, this is very interesting because in English, we don't have that many counting words, measure words.
segments.zh: 现在，这很有趣，因为在英语中，我们没有那么多计数单词，测量单词。

segments.en: Right.
But for bread, we do actually have this special word.
segments.zh: 但对于面包，我们确实有这个特殊的词。

segments.en: So, you can say, I would like two loaves of sourdough bread.
segments.zh: 所以，你可以说，我想要两条酸面团面包。

segments.en: Okay.
And a loaf or loaves in the plural, what is it exactly?
segments.zh: loaf，复数形式是 loaves，它到底是什么？

segments.en: It's one big piece.
So, for example, you have maybe one little piece of bread.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，您可能有一小块面包。

segments.en: It's called a slice.
That's what you eat.
But when you buy the bread, you have many, many, many slices together.
segments.zh: 但是当你买面包的时候，你有很多很多很多的切片放在一起。

segments.en: Before you cut the bread, that's called a loaf.
segments.zh: 在你切面包之前，那叫做一条面包。

segments.en: Very good.
And this is the reason why the baker or the person attending the shop asked if he would like to have the loaf sliced.
segments.zh: 这就是面包师或接待的店员问他是否要把这条面包切片的原因。

segments.en: Would you like the loaf sliced?
That means, would you like us to cut pieces of bread from this loaf?
segments.zh: 这意味着，你想让我们从这条面包上切面包片吗？

segments.en: Because sliced bread is how you eat it.
segments.zh: 因为切片面包是你吃的方式。

segments.en: Right.
Exactly.
You don't really take a whole loaf of bread and start eating it like that.
segments.zh: 你不会真拿一整条面包就那么啃起来。

segments.en: Like an animal.
No.
You cut it into slices.
So, sliced bread, we say, is one option.
segments.zh: 因此，我们说，切片面包是一种选择。

segments.en: You can also have unsliced, which means when you go home, you cut it yourself.
segments.zh: 你也可以要不切片的，也就是回家后自己切。

segments.en: So this is a very particular word as well because you have the adjective to have sliced bread.
segments.zh: 所以这也是一个非常特别的词，因为你有切片面包的形容词。

segments.en: You also have the verb to slice the bread.
That means to cut it into slices.
And of course, you have the noun slices of bread.
So you have the individual pieces.
segments.zh: 所以你有单独的一片片。

segments.en: So it can be a verb, an adjective, and a noun.
segments.zh: 所以它可以是动词、形容词和名词。

segments.en: That's right.
It can be a little confusing, but I recommend you all check out the website and practice a little bit in the comments section.
segments.zh: 这可能有点令人困惑，但我建议大家查看网站并在评论部分练习一点。

segments.en: All right.
Good.
So let's take a listen to the dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 所以让我们最后一次听一听对话。

segments.en: Welcome to Al's Bakery.
What can I get you?
Hi.
Let me get a dozen croissants, four blueberry muffins, and a loaf of sourdough bread.
segments.zh: 让我买一打羊角面包、四个蓝莓松饼和一条酸面包。

segments.en: Sure.
Would you like to have the loaf sliced?
No, that's okay.
Do you have any whole wheat bread?
Oh, we're out at the moment.
May I suggest some rye bread?
Sure.
That sounds good.
Do you have any cakes?
We have various birthday cakes and also some ice cream cakes.
segments.zh: 我们有各种生日蛋糕和一些冰淇淋蛋糕。

segments.en: I'll just take a cheesecake.
Will that be all?
Yes.
Your total is $43.20.
All right.
So speaking about breads now, there is some particular ingredients that we don't mention in the dialogue, obviously.
segments.zh: 那说到面包，有些特别的配料我们在对话里显然没有提到。

segments.en: But they're worth mentioning, what is the one main characteristic that most breads have?
segments.zh: 但值得一提的是，大多数面包的主要特征是什么？

segments.en: Yeast.
Yeast.
That's right.
Y-E-A-S-T.
Yeast.
And yeast is actually alive.
It's an animal.
It's like a bacteria.
That's right.
And so you wonder why are some breads flat and why are some breads big, poofy, large?
segments.zh: 所以你会想，为什么有些面包是扁平的，有些却又大又蓬松？

segments.en: Well, yeast is why.
Basically, you can't have a big poofy bread, a big, large, tall bread, unless you have this yeast.
segments.zh: 基本上，没有这种酵母，你就做不出蓬松的大面包，又大又高的面包。

segments.en: So yeast is what makes the bread rise.
segments.zh: 所以酵母是使面包上升的原因。

segments.en: Yes.
And we also mentioned flour, which is basically just a powder made out of some type of grain usually.
segments.zh: 我们还提到了面粉，它基本上只是一种由某种谷物制成的粉末。

segments.en: Yeah.
Usually it's made out of wheat.
Obviously, whole wheat is a little bit different from the white flour, which would be a different processed wheat.
segments.zh: 显然，全麦与白面粉有点不同，白面粉是另一种加工过的小麦。

segments.en: But we also have different things that you can even have rice flour.
segments.zh: 但我们也有别的，比如还可以用米粉。

segments.en: Right.
Corn flour.
Corn flour.
So corn bread would be, of course, yellow because corn is yellow.
segments.zh: 所以玉米面包当然会是黄色的，因为玉米是黄色的。

segments.en: Now, so you can hear that we say the word flour like a rose is a flower, but it's actually spelled different.
segments.zh: 你可以听到，我们说的 flour 和 a rose is a flower 里的 flower 发音一样，但拼写不同。

segments.en: F-L-O-U-R, flour.
So there's two different things.
segments.zh: 所以有两个不同的东西。

segments.en: There's flours in your garden and there's flour, F-L-O-U-R, which is something you can cook with.
segments.zh: 你花园里有的是 flowers（花），而 flour，F-L-O-U-R，是做饭用的东西。

segments.en: That's right.
These are called homophones.
So they basically have the same pronunciation, but very different spellings.
segments.zh: 所以它们基本上有相同的发音，但拼写非常不同。

segments.en: And very different meanings.
Exactly.
So a very interesting lesson for us today.
segments.zh: 所以今天对我们来说是很有意思的一课。

segments.en: Go out, get some bread, try some of these if you have them available.
segments.zh: 出去，买些面包，如果有的话，可以试试这些。

segments.en: But also, come to the questions and comments section and tell us about maybe your local bread.
segments.zh: 此外，请访问问题和评论部分，告诉我们可能是您当地的面包。

segments.en: I know that many countries around the world have very specific types of bread.
segments.zh: 我知道世界上许多国家都有非常具体的面包类型。

segments.en: That's right.
Write some names down for us, send us your pictures, and we'll see you on the website.
segments.zh: 为我们写下一些名字，将您的照片发送给我们，我们将在网站上见到您。

segments.en: All right.
Bye, guys.
